featured_reviews.review_text:
My 15-Day Ear Treatment Journey

I want to share my experience because it might help someone facing the same problem.

It started when I had severe pain in my ear and didn’t know what to do. I decided to put a few drops of oil in my ear. After two days, the pain went away, and I felt fine. But soon after, a new problem started my ear became completely clogged with wax, and I couldn’t hear anything. I thought it would clear up on its own, but even after 10 days, there was no improvement.

I got really worried and started searching online for solutions. I tried several exercises and remedies I found on Google, but nothing helped. It was a very difficult time because I could only hear from one ear. Finally, I decided to visit an ENT specialist.

I searched for nearby ENT clinics and, after reading reviews, I booked an appointment at Dr. Dipali’s Clinic.

When I met Dr. Dipali, I explained everything to her. She examined my right ear and said that there was wax buildup that needed to be removed. She cleaned my ear, and within 10 minutes, it was completely open  I could finally hear clearly again! I was so happy at that moment.

However, soon after, I noticed a new issue  a constant beeping sound in my ear, known as tinnitus. It was very disturbing and made it hard to sleep, focus, or concentrate. I went back to Dr. Dipali, and she prescribed some medicines for the tinnitus.

After 15 days of treatment, the beeping sound completely disappeared. I’m so grateful to Dr. Dipali for her care and support.

Thank you very much, Dr. Dipali and your clinic!
I highly recommend this clinic to anyone who needs ear treatment.

What Are Tonsils?

Tonsils are part of the body's immune system and help protect against germs entering through the mouth and nose. They play an important role, especially during childhood.

Viral infections (most common)

Bacterial infections such as strep throat

Allergies and post-nasal drip

Acid reflux (LPR)

Environmental irritants such as smoke and pollution.

Not every sore throat requires antibiotics. Proper diagnosis is essential to identify the cause and ensure appropriate treatment. Recurrent throat infections, persistent symptoms, or breathing difficulties should never be ignored.

A tiny fish bone, a major surgical challenge, and a valuable lesson in timely diagnosis.

I recently had the opportunity to  manage  a rare and complex case involving an 11-year-old girl who presented with persistent throat pain and difficulty swallowing after a fish meal.

What initially appeared to be a routine fish bone impaction turned out to be far more serious. Advanced imaging revealed that the fish bone had perforated the food pipe and migrated into the thyroid gland, leading to a deep neck infection and abscess formation.

The case required careful planning and open neck surgery to safely remove the foreign body while preserving critical structures responsible for voice function and calcium regulation.

I am pleased that the patient made an excellent recovery and has returned to her normal activities.

Cases like these remind us that: 

 Persistent symptoms should never be dismissed.

 Advanced imaging can be crucial when routine examinations are inconclusive.




 Early referral to an ENT specialist can prevent potentially serious complications.
